findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:151 — Backup-code consumption uses a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing concurrent logins to reuse the same code or overwrite updates and restore consumed codes. Use an atomic conditional update and reject or retry conflicts.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it. Keep the button keyboard-focusable.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

Use an atomic conditional update and reject or retry conflicts.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - the non-atomic read-modify-write pattern for backup codes that allows concurrent login requests to reuse the same backup code. Both comments point out that the backup codes are read, modified in memory, and written back without proper atomicity, which could allow a single backup code to be used multiple times in concurrent requests. The candidate even suggests the same type of fix (atomic conditional update).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it. Keep the button keyboard-focusable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows tabIndex={-1} being added to the password visibility toggle button in PasswordField. This removes the button from keyboard tab navigation, which is an accessibility issue. Keyboard-only users would not be able to reach this button to toggle password visibility. This is a real accessibility bug introduced by this change.
